sections: Toowoomba Referral Group (TRG) is a business networking community that builds strong relationships and generates high-quality business leads in a supportive, structured environment.
With a strong community spirit, TRG also raises significant funds for local charities through its popular annual charity golf event.

Beyond business, members enjoy a vibrant social calendar—optional events include free breakfasts, Christmas in July, Christmas Trivia, and an end-of-year Christmas Party, creating a fun, connected, and engaged group culture.

raffle.heading: TRG 2026 Charity Golf Day Major Prize
raffle.body: The Toowoomba Referral Group is hosting its charity golf day again in November 2026. Participants will have the chance to win a major cash prize of $5,000. Join us for a day of golf and support a good cause. Tickets are only $10 each and can be purchased online.

cards.title: Business Promotion
items: At the the beginning of every meeting, each TRG member is allocated 60 seconds to promote their business.
Members are also invited and scheduled to prepare and deliver 20 minute presentations on their products and services at least twice during the calendar year.
Network with other members before, during and after the meeting to discuss ideas and exchange information and professional advice.
Participate in association sponsored activities and events.

cards.title: Member Benefits
items: Generate and receive quality business leads and referrals.
Be inspired, motivated and increase your knowledge base from our guest speakers.
Receive support and actively promote other business owners and managers.
Be equipped with business tools for self-confidence and business development.
Build confidence in the delivery of your product/service.
Be part of an environment which encourages brainstorming.

cards.title: Who Can Join?
items: Any person who wants to increase business success by meeting with other people for the purpose of giving and receiving quality referrals.
Any person who gives without expecting something in return.
A member must have a reputation for good business ethics.
There is only one member per business category.
Each member is approved by the management committee to ensure quality of membership is maintained.

body: Toowoomba Referral Group is a business referral group which focuses on providing business networking and business leads within a structured and positive environment.

/community.heading: In the Community

seo.title: TRG in the Community | Supporting Toowoomba’s Growth and Local Initiatives
seo.description: TRG supports local Toowoomba community and charity events.

body: TRG has long been a proud supporter of the Toowoomba region, investing time, resources, and expertise to help the community thrive. From sponsoring local events and sporting clubs to collaborating with schools and charities, TRG takes an active role in creating opportunities that strengthen the city's social and economic fabric.
Their involvement goes beyond business—it's about fostering connections and supporting the people who make Toowoomba such a vibrant place to live and work.

Through partnerships with local organisations, TRG champions initiatives that drive education, sustainability, and innovation. Whether it's contributing to community development projects, backing local entrepreneurs, or supporting youth programs, TRG continually seeks to make a lasting difference. Their focus on empowering local talent and nurturing future leaders reflects a deep belief in Toowoomba's potential and resilience.

TRG's ongoing presence in the Toowoomba community demonstrates their unwavering commitment to giving back. By aligning their values with the needs of the region, they continue to build meaningful relationships and contribute to a stronger, more connected community.
As Toowoomba continues to grow, TRG remains dedicated to playing its part—investing in people, supporting local success, and helping shape a brighter future for generations to come.

seo.title: TRG Annual Charity Golf Day | Swing for a Cause
seo.description: The TRG Charity Golf Day raises funds for local Toowoomba charities.

intro: The TRG Charity Golf Day is an annual community event hosted by the Toowoomba Referral Group to raise funds for two local charities.
Held at the picturesque Toowoomba Golf Club, it’s a day where local businesses, sponsors, and players come together for a round of golf, good food, and great company — all for a worthy cause.

With team registrations, hole sponsorships, and prizes throughout the day, the eventblends friendly competition with genuine community spirit, helping make adifference for local families affected by cancer and serious injury.

sponsorships: All other sponsorship opportunities are currently exhausted

charities.name: Hope Horizons
charities.body: Hope Horizons Cancer Wellness Centre opened its doors in Toowoomba, Southeast Queensland in 2017. Born from a desire to see free allied health services provided for those living with cancer in the region, while ever cancer remains, our mission is to diminish its impact.

charities.name: Maddox's Helping Hand
charities.body: Maddox's Helping Hand Foundation (MHHF) was established in 2020 and supports ACCISS where the public hospital system cannot. In May 2021 MHHF held its first fundraising event and has since raised almost $700,000.

seo.title: Precinct | Urban Planners in Toowoomba
seo.description: Precinct Urban Planning is a boutique town planning consultancy practice offering specialist services in statutory and strategic planning and development management. Based in the dynamic western growth corridor, with offices in Toowoomba and Ipswich

body: Precinct Urban Planning personnel have extensive experience in strategic, statutory and specialist town planning and management consulting services and provide timely, accurate and strategically astute advice focussed on individual client needs. The practice values experience, provides insight and delivers workable planning solutions.

James is a qualified town planner, having completed a Bachelor of Planning degree at James Cook University (JCU) in Townsville, North Queensland, graduating in 2018. His studies involved a number of practical courses including Indigenous Environmental Management, Environmental and Regional Planning, and Urban Design.

James has over seven (7) years’ experience within the private sector. Prior to joining Precinct Urban Planning in early 2019, James previously worked as a Planner for a building certification company in Townsville. In addition to assessing proposed developments in rural and regional Queensland against the relevant planning requirements, this position also allowed him to understand and implement building legislation, such as the Building Act 1975 and Queensland Development Code.

Since becoming a member of the Precinct team, James has gained a wealth of knowledge and experience, working on a range of developments from small-scale uses such as Airbnbs, dwellings and offices to large-scale uses such as poultry farms, schools, hospitals and community facilities. He has also benefitted by assisting local governments in the assessment of various types of Development Applications.

In these roles, James has developed the knowledge to provide accurate and succinct planning advice for an array of residential, commercial, industrial and rural projects in a range of council regions across Queensland, New South Wales and Western Australia.

Additionally, James has worked on projects of regional and state significance, including Ministerial and Local Government Infrastructure Designations for the redevelopment of the Toowoomba Hospital and other large scale projects such as hospitals, schools, electricity infrastructure and dams.

body: If you’ve ever heard whispers that the Toowoomba Referral Group Charity Golf Day is something special, consider this your confirmation.

Our annual Charity Golf Day was nothing short of incredible. From the first tee-off to the final putt, the day was packed with laughs, generosity, community spirit, and (let’s be honest) a few creative golf swings.
Thanks to the overwhelming support of our sponsors, golfers, volunteers, and donors, we’re proud to share that we raised an incredible:
$32,803.70 for charity
Not only did we beat last year’s total, we absolutely smashed it.
All funds raised will be shared evenly between two very deserving charities:
These funds will make a genuine, tangible difference in the lives of individuals and families in our community, and we couldn’t be more grateful to everyone who played a part.
While the golf itself was… entertaining (accuracy was optional), the real highlight of the day was the atmosphere.
From generous sponsors and prize donors to volunteers who kept everything running smoothly, and golfers who brought the fun and the heart, the TRG community showed up in the best possible way.
It was a reminder of what can happen when local businesses and individuals come together with a shared purpose: to give back, support those who need it most, and enjoy the process along the way.
To every sponsor, donor, golfer, volunteer, and supporter — thank you. Your generosity, energy, and willingness to get involved are what make this event bigger and better every year.
You are truly the best team we’ve ever teed up with.

/trg-guest-jesse-mccartney-from-belong-i.heading: TRG Guest: Jesse McCartney from Belong in Hockey

seo.title: TRG Guest: Jesse McCartney from Belong in Hockey
seo.description: TRG was inspired to hear from Jessie McCartney, co-founder of award-winning initiative Belong in Hockey — a Toowoomba program using sport to support refugees and build community connections.

body: We were delighted to welcome Jessie McCartney to our Wednesday morning meeting to share the story behind Belong in Hockey. And what a story it is.

Belong in Hockey is an award-winning, Toowoomba-based initiative founded by Jessie and Elizabeth Laverty that uses the power of sport to support refugees, particularly Yazidi families, as they settle into life in our community. Through weekly training sessions — now expanded to include Saturdays — the program builds far more than hockey skills. It fosters confidence, community connection, and even English proficiency along the way.

It's the kind of initiative that reminds you just how much a simple game can change lives. Jessie's passion for the people behind the program was infectious, and it's no surprise that Belong in Hockey has earned award recognition for the incredible work they do.
We left the meeting feeling genuinely inspired by what Jessie and Elizabeth have built right here in Toowoomba.
If you would like more information regarding the program, please email Jessie, the Hockey Manager, at hockeymanager@toowoombahockey.com.au

/toowoomba’s-own-kevin-howarth-rings-out.heading: Toowoomba’s Own Kevin Howarth Rings Out Success at the Australian Town Crier Championships

seo.title: Toowoomba’s Own Kevin Howarth Rings Out Success at the Australian Town Crier Championships
seo.description: Australia’s Loudest Crier is from Toowoomba! Kevin Howarth takes home four major awards, showcasing his dedication and pride in the local community.

body: At the 36th National Town Crier Championships held in Canberra, Kevin delivered a standout performance, taking home four national titles, including Australia’s Loudest Crier, Best Cry, Best Media Campaign, and the prestigious Pat Adamson Memorial Award for Best Regional Ambassador.

Despite challenging conditions — with gusty winds toppling shade shelters and sending tricorn hats flying — Kevin’s dedication and spirit shone through. “I’ve competed in many events over the years, but Canberra’s wind made this one particularly memorable,” Kevin said with a grin.“Crying into the wind was tricky for everyone, but the effort was worth it. The job satisfaction I get from representing Toowoomba and sharing our story with others is incredible.”

Kevin’s “loudest cry” reached 92 decibels on the day — slightly below his usual competition level of over 100 decibels, but still strong enough to defend his title for another year. He previously claimed the same honour in 2018, 2019, and 2023.

As the Toowoomba Region’s official Town Crier, Kevin proudly represents the community at events big and small — from citizenship ceremonies and centenarian birthdays to major festivals and civic celebrations.
